data.gender_notes: Hieronymus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'hieros' meaning 'sacred' and 'onymos' meaning 'name', Hieronymus is an honorary name given to the holy. This name has been borne by several saints, including Saint Jerome, who translated the Bible into Latin. The name Hieronymus carries the meaning “Honorary name of the Holy” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Hieronymus usually hope their child will grow to embody honorary name of the holy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes dedication and commitment to the divine.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hieronymus total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hieronymus has its roots in ancient Rome and signifies an individual deeply committed to religious learning and scholarship, especially in the area of Scripture. The name carries a rich historical legacy and is reminiscent of the esteemed work of Saint Jerome, whose contributions to spiritual and intellectual pursuits have influenced Western Christianity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hieronymus is laden with profound spiritual significance. It not only signifies a connection to the divine, but also reflects a commitment to deep study and understanding of sacred texts. As a result, a person named Hieronymus may be inspiring and revered as a spiritual authority figure. The name holds a special meaning in the Christian faith, being closely linked to the devotion and dedication embodied by Saint Jerome and his invaluable contributions to the Bible.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hieronymus, derived from Greek hieros (sacred) and romanos (Roman), symbolizes a sacred or holy Roman. Spiritually, it represents a commitment to upholding Christian values in the secular Roman world.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Hieronymus is mentioned in the writings of St. Jerome The name Hieronymus carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Hieronymus is a Latinized form of the Greek name Hieronymos, and was used to refer to the Christian theologian and biblical scholar St. Jerome
